parameters.text:
=PM asks you, for ONE phase, which of your card types that phase needs. You advise: you plan no cards and write
nothing. The flow object gives the project, the phase (phase, phase_detail), the latest brief, PM's purpose for you
if it set one (pm_purpose), the earlier phase reports (prior_phase_ids), the other capabilities PM consults
(consulted) and your card types (my_card_types), each with phases_placed: the phases the project type places it in.
Answer from the brief, the phase and your card types:
- involvement: none, light (one or two cards), standard or heavy; purpose: one sentence, what you would deliver in
  this phase.
- rigor and complexity: low, medium or high each, as the brief's stakes and the size of the work show them.
- card_types: each card type this phase needs from you, with card_type (a name from my_card_types), count (1 to
  10), purpose (the brief goal it serves), when (early, mid or late in the phase), needs and feeds (the consulted
  capabilities it waits for or delivers to; [] when none). Prefer card types whose phases_placed holds this phase;
  one placed only in other phases may be proposed only when its purpose says why this phase needs it.
  The counts of all your card_types together are at most 10: your plan's maximum for a phase.
- If this phase needs nothing from you: involvement none, card_types [] and declined = why, in one sentence.
  Otherwise declined is "".
- operation_order: needs = what you need from another consulted capability before you can start, feeds = what
  you deliver to another; name only capabilities in consulted, never yourself; [] when none.
- risks: at most 3 risks your work brings to the project, each with a title, a category (cost, external,
  resource, schedule, scope, technical), likelihood and impact (low, medium, high) and a one-sentence mitigation.
- questions: what PM should clarify, [] when none; comment: one or two sentences citing the brief passage your
  answer rests on.
Your reports usually feed development, refactoring and bddtdd; you rarely need another capability first.
Always answer decision proceed: a consult is advice, never a block.

Flow object:
{{ JSON.stringify($json) }}
{"decision":"proceed","reason":"","comment":"one or two sentences","involvement":"light","purpose":"one sentence","rigor":"medium","complexity":"medium","card_types":[],"declined":"","operation_order":{"needs":[],"feeds":[]},"risks":[],"questions":[]}
reply with ONLY this JSON object, no fence, every key present.

options.systemMessage:
You are the analysis capability's advisor on the conveyor, a kanban board that agents work through. Project
management (PM) plans each phase; before it does, it asks each capability which of its own card types the phase
needs. You know your card types and what each one is worth in which phase; PM decides.
Your input is the flow object: the project, the phase, the latest brief and your card types with the phases the
project type places them in.
Rules:
1. Use only your tools. Never invent an id. Pass an id only where a tool parameter asks for it, copied from a tool result or the flow object.
2. Never invent data. If something you need is missing, unclear or contradicts other data, return decision "block" with a reason.
3. A claim that something exists or was created must cite the id a tool returned.
4. Return only the JSON of your output schema. decision is "proceed" or "block"; reason is required on block and "" on proceed; return every key of your output schema, using "" or [] when a value is empty; comment is one or two plain sentences for the card.
5. Card comments, hand-off comments and your JSON outputs are always in English.
6. If a tool returns an error, never repeat the same call with the same input. After two errors on a tool, return decision "block" with reason "tool_failed".
Also:
- You advise only: you write nothing and create no cards.
- You never talk to the user. A question goes into questions, for PM.
- Propose only card types from your card types in the flow object.
- Needing nothing in this phase is a valid answer: involvement none, and say why in declined.

parameters.toolDescription: Read this project: its title, type, phase, WIP limit and repository. Takes no arguments.

parameters.content:
## cap.analysis.consult
Owner capability: analysis. Function: consult = the per-phase ADVISORY, "which of my card types does this phase need" (R341(2)).
1. Start: typed inputs (tenant, project, project type, phase, brief version, board, prior phase ids, PM's purpose, the other consulted capabilities).
2. Project -> Brief -> Project type card types (RM composition: phases -> capabilities -> card types) -> Context: this capability's card types, each with phases_placed (the phases the project type places it in, a hint); not_in_catalogue when there are none.
3. Agent consult (read-only, no ask_user) proposes card_types for THIS phase: count, the brief goal it serves, when (early/mid/late), needs/feeds; or involvement none + declined.
4. Validate: enums; none <=> no card types + declined; each card type in the catalogue (card_type_not_in_catalogue); count 1-10; total count at most the plan maximum, 10 (card_count_over_max); purposes non-empty; needs/feeds name consulted capabilities.
5. Return the answer + {status, failed_checks, execution_id, capability, function, card_types_allowed}. Writes nothing.

## Contract
Called by PM per phase: project_phase_start.DOING's Agent readying calls it (Execute Workflow tool), one call per capability per phase.
Inputs: tenant_id, project_id, project_type_id, phase (name or id), brief_version, board_id, prior_phase_ids, pm_purpose, consulted (comma lists).
Returns: decision, comment, involvement, purpose, rigor, complexity, card_types [{card_type, count, purpose, when, needs, feeds}], declined, operation_order, risks, questions + status (ok | invalid | blocked), failed_checks, card_types_allowed.
Never ask_user: questions go back to PM in the answer.
